subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Chiplets: The Future of Chip Design
description: A micro-lesson that makes Chiplets: The Future of Chip Design usable.

hook.text: Why make one giant chip when you can connect many small ones? That's the chiplet idea.

buildup.text: Each chiplet handles one function: CPU, GPU, memory, I/O. They connect on a shared substrate.

discovery.text: Smaller dies have higher yields. Mixing process nodes saves cost and boosts flexibility.

twist.text: AMD's EPYC server chips use chiplets to outperform monolithic designs at lower cost.

climax.text: Industry standards like UCIe let chiplets from different companies work together.

punchline.text: Small chips, big performance — chiplets are LEGO bricks for processors.

quiz.question: What is a key advantage of chiplet-based designs?
options: They eliminate the need for transistors entirely
Smaller dies have higher manufacturing yields, reducing cost
Chiplets don't require any interconnect technology
